gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the makers' 'surge' numbers on one footing: BLUETTI's 2,700 W (Elite 100 V2, AC180) and 2,250 W (Pioneer Na) are 'Lifting Power', a mode BLUETTI pitches for heating devices, while ALLPOWERS's 3,600 W on the P1800 is a 'peak' figure. Nor does any say that the '1,000 W solar input, full charge in 70 mins' line on BLUETTI's Elite 100 V2 + 200 W kit page assumes five times the panel that ships in the box (1,024 Wh / 200 W = 5.1 h of full sun at rated output).
standout_why: I could open only one rival page in full: StormWatts (cited; read 2026-11-17). It lists each kit's battery Wh, solar-input cap and voltage window, and it explains its refill planning model (4.5 sun-hours, 0.85 efficiency). It gives no surge or continuous AC rating, no cycle life and no end-of-life %, so the surge-vs-lifting finding is new against it. The solar-cap half of the finding is partly there already. I could not open three other rival pages, two of them cited: unpluggedwatts.com and theoutageready.com (cited; WebFetch cert error, curl not allowed) and the cited solargenreview.com AC180 review (HTTP 429). I also could not open agentretrievalindex.com or solargenadvisor.com (cert errors). I scored 1 instead of 2 because I could not check the cited pages. If those pages also leave out cycle-life end points and lifting vs surge, this is a 2.
decides: It confirms a pick and does not change it. Among kits we link at 800–1,200 Wh, the ones that ship now are: ALLPOWERS P1800 + 600 W ($718.20 link price, $798.00 store), the BLUETTI Elite 100 mini kits (700 W AC) and the BLUETTI Pioneer Na + 200 W and + 2× 200 W kits. The cheaper P1800 + 200 W, Elite 100 V2 and AC180 kits are pre-orders. P1800 + 600 W wins the ships-now slot. Its 600 W of panels sits under the station's 650 W solar input (1,024 Wh / 600 W = 1.7 h of full sun at rated output). Its 1,800 W rated AC is the same as the Elite 100 V2 and AC180. The table should compare the 1,800 W rated figure and footnote the rest: '3,600 W peak' (ALLPOWERS) is not the same thing as '2,700 W lifting' (BLUETTI). The table should also list each kit's own panel watts next to the station's solar cap, so a 1,000 W input headline doesn't make a 100–200 W kit look like it refills in about an hour. The pre-order alternatives are the Elite 100 V2 + 200 W ($692.55 link price, ships mid-December 2026; 4,000+ cycles to 80% on BLUETTI's page) and the AC180 + 200 W (ships Dec 14, 2026; 3,500+ cycles to 80%).
